meta: A Dutch navy ship fires a salute in Willem van de Velde the Younger's The Gun Salute, painted around 1680 and now in the Rijksmuseum.
about: A ship of the Dutch navy fires a gun salute. Willem van de Velde the Younger painted it around 1680, after he moved to England, and it has a pendant, The Gust of Wind. A banker named Adriaan van der Hoop bought it in 1834. He thought it showed De Zeven Provinciën, the flagship of Michiel de Ruyter, but that identification has since been refuted. A critic gave it its present title in 1845. The Rijksmuseum has had it since 1885.

meta: A farmer with a pitchfork stands beside his daughter in front of a Gothic-windowed house in Grant Wood's American Gothic, painted in 1930.
about: A farmer in overalls and a suit jacket holds a pitchfork beside a woman in a colonial print apron. Behind them is a small white house with a pointed Gothic window. Grant Wood saw the house in Eldon, Iowa, in 1930 and decided to paint it together with the kind of people he thought should live there. His sister Nan and the family dentist, Byron McKeeby, posed for the figures. The painting belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.

meta: Titian's Madonna of the Roses, painted around 1530, shows Mary and the Child with Saint Anthony and a young John the Baptist.
about: Mary and the Christ Child sit with Anthony the Great and a young John the Baptist in this panel by Titian. It was painted around 1530 and is signed Ticianus f., although the signature may have been added later. Archduke Leopold Wilhelm of Austria once owned it. In 1793 it was sent from Vienna to Florence in a swap that also brought Titian's Flora and a Dürer to the city. It is now in the Uffizi.

meta: Botticelli's Last Communion of Saint Jerome, finished around 1495 for Francesco del Pugliese, a follower of Savonarola, now in the Met.
about: Saint Jerome lies on a linen sheet, surrounded by the brothers of his monastery, and asks to receive the body of Christ. Botticelli finished the painting around 1494 or 1495. No ancient author is known to have described this scene. It comes from a medieval letter that was reprinted often in Italy by the 1480s. Francesco del Pugliese, a follower of Savonarola, ordered it. The scholar Rita Lizzi Testa links the subject to Savonarola's preaching in Florence. It is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

meta: Perugino's Saint Sebastian from about 1507, thought to be his own near-identical copy of the version in the Louvre.
about: Saint Sebastian is the subject of this painting by Perugino from about 1507. It is thought to be his own copy of a version now in the Louvre. The two are nearly identical, except that this one lacks the inscription and the ruins of the Paris picture. It is in the São Paulo Museum of Art.

meta: Fishermen launch a boat in Oscar Björck's 1884 painting, the largest of his open-air works from Skagen.
about: Local fishermen go about their work as they launch a boat. The Swedish artist Oscar Björck painted the scene in 1884, and Wikipedia says it is the largest of his open-air paintings from Skagen. The fishermen of the Danish town were a favourite subject for the Skagen Painters. The picture is on display in Skagens Museum.

meta: Cornplanter, a Seneca leader, holding a pipe and axe blades in a colour lithograph by J.T. Bowen after F. Bartoli, 1836.
about: Cornplanter holds a smoking pipe with attachments and axe blades in this colour lithograph by J.T. Bowen after F. Bartoli, from 1836. Cornplanter lived from about 1732 to 1836. According to the University of Cincinnati Libraries, he was a leader of the Seneca Nation, together with Red Jacket. The print is in the Wellcome Collection.

meta: Pier Leone Ghezzi as the knight of caricature, in an etching by Carl Marcus Tuscher of 1743, with a poster-covered statue behind him.
about: Pier Leone Ghezzi stands with a stick and both hands raised, shown in the manner of his own drawings. Behind him is a statue on a plinth, covered in posters and in caricatures like the ones Ghezzi made. The plinth is inscribed Artes cui mille, meaning who has a thousand ways. Carl Marcus Tuscher made the etching in 1743. It is in the Wellcome Collection.

meta: A blue foal faces the viewer in Franz Marc's Blue Horse I, painted in 1911 and now in the Lenbachhaus in Munich.
about: A blue foal fills almost the whole canvas, facing us with its head tilted a little to one side. Its body is light blue with white spots, and its mane and hooves are dark navy. Franz Marc painted it in 1911, working up a postcard sized pencil sketch. In the thinking of the Blue Rider group, blue stood for the spiritual. At first people did not understand the picture. Some derided it. It has hung in the Lenbachhaus in Munich since 1965.

meta: Members of the Vendramin family kneel at an altar with a relic of the True Cross in Titian's group portrait of the early 1540s.
about: Members of the Vendramin family kneel at an altar that holds a reliquary of the True Cross. Titian and his workshop painted the group in the early 1540s, and as was usual in Venice it shows only the men. Wikipedia says the brothers Andrea and Gabriele are here with Andrea's sons, but nobody is sure which brother is which. The three small boys on the left were added later by another artist and are much weaker. The relic still exists, and the family's confraternity still holds it.

meta: A girl in a blue dress, her name unknown: Johannes Cornelisz. Verspronck's portrait of 1641, in the Rijksmuseum since 1928.
about: Nobody knows who the girl in the blue dress was, or who her family was. Johannes Cornelisz. Verspronck painted her in 1641, and her pose is close to that of a marriage portrait he had made the year before. In 1923 a consortium of the Vereniging Rembrandt bought works from the collection of the Grand Duke of Oldenburg, and the chairman Mari Paul Voûte took this one. He kept it until he died. It then passed to the Rijksmuseum in 1928.

meta: An alchemist kneels before a shining vessel as he discovers phosphorus in Joseph Wright of Derby's painting of 1771, reworked in 1795.
about: An alchemist searching for the Philosopher's Stone kneels before a shining vessel and finds phosphorus instead. Joseph Wright of Derby finished the picture in 1771 and reworked it in 1795. Wikipedia says it may allude to Hennig Brand, the Hamburg alchemist who found phosphorus in 1669, a story often printed in popular chemistry books. Wright put the laboratory under medieval arches with tall pointed windows, like a church. His friend Peter Perez Burdett sketched the layout and fixed where the figure should stand.

meta: The Virgin and Child sit among six saints, two of them probably Medici portraits, in Sandro Botticelli's Sant'Ambrogio Altarpiece of about 1470.
about: The Virgin sits enthroned with the Christ Child among six saints. They are Mary Magdalene, John the Baptist, Francis of Assisi, Catherine of Alexandria and, kneeling, Cosmas and Damian. Cosmas and Damian were the patron saints of the Medici, and Wikipedia says they are most likely portraits of Medici family members, with Lorenzo the Magnificent and his brother Giuliano suggested. Sandro Botticelli finished the Sant'Ambrogio Altarpiece around 1470, and it hangs in the Uffizi.

meta: A banjo player breaks into planes of black, white, yellow and red in Albert Gleizes's Composition for Jazz, made in New York in 1915.
about: A banjo player and a second figure emerge from broad overlapping planes of black, white, yellow and red. Albert Gleizes made Composition for Jazz in New York in 1915, in gouache on cardboard. Wikipedia says the head of the musician on the left sits oddly on top of his body, as if the whole picture were an improvised memory of a jazz performance. Solomon Guggenheim bought it in 1938, and it is now in the Guggenheim collection.

meta: Emily Carr painted a church at Friendly Cove in 1929, and Lawren Harris bought it for his dining room and called it her best work.
about: Emily Carr painted this church at Friendly Cove, near a lighthouse. Lawren Harris bought it for his dining room and called it her best work. When Carr saw it in his home she said the house must have bewitched it, because it looked better than she had thought. She could not keep looking while people praised it. It was shown at the National Gallery of Canada and later at the Tate Gallery in 1938. The Art Gallery of Ontario renamed it Church at Yuquot Village in 2018.

meta: Leonardo's Leda and the Swan survives only in copies, and this one in the Uffizi, dated about 1505 to 1507, is counted among the closest.
about: Leonardo's own Leda is lost. Three paintings count as the closest copies of it, and this one in the Uffizi is among them. Bernard Berenson thought Leonardo painted it himself, but modern art historians reject that and favor one of his students, possibly Francesco Melzi, with some help from Joos van Cleve on the landscape background. The date is to about 1505 to 1507, and the Uffizi bought it from the Spiridon collection in 1989.

meta: Mary holds the child with two angels in a marble enclosure in Andrea del Verrocchio's Virgin and Child, painted about 1467 to 1469.
about: Mary holds the child on her lap with the help of two baby angels. They sit in a marble enclosure that points to the hortus conclusus, the enclosed garden, and a stylized landscape lies behind. Andrea del Verrocchio painted it between about 1467 and 1469. Wikipedia says the theme comes from the Madonnas of Filippo Lippi, and that Botticelli took it up in a Madonna now in Naples. The National Gallery in London owns Verrocchio's picture.

meta: Galeazzo Maria Sforza in the blue brocade he wore entering Florence in 1471: Piero del Pollaiuolo's portrait in the Uffizi.
about: Galeazzo Maria Sforza wears the blue brocade with lilies that chroniclers say he had on when he rode into Florence on 13 March 1471. Piero del Pollaiuolo painted him that year, during his third visit to strengthen an alliance with Lorenzo the Magnificent. A restoration in 1994 showed that the paint went straight onto an unprepared panel, in the Flemish manner. Wikipedia says it may once have been paired with a portrait of Federico da Montefeltro. Both are listed in Lorenzo's room in an inventory of 1492.

meta: Pontormo's portrait of Giovanni della Casa, author of Galateo, painted in the early 1540s and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
about: The sitter was long called Niccolò Ardinghelli but is now thought to be Giovanni della Casa, who wrote Galateo. Pontormo painted the portrait in the early 1540s. In 1909 it was sold in Paris as a work by Sebastiano del Piombo. After several owners it went to the Kress Foundation in 1952, and the foundation gave it to the National Gallery of Art in Washington in 1961.

meta: Napoleon stands at the gangway of HMS Bellerophon as a prisoner off Plymouth in Charles Lock Eastlake's 1815 painting.
about: Napoleon stands at the gangway of HMS Bellerophon in the uniform of a colonel of chasseurs, a prisoner of the British off Plymouth. He had surrendered to the ship on 14 July 1815, after trying to reach the United States. Crowds gathered on the shore, and Charles Lock Eastlake, a young and little known artist, hired a boat and rowed out to study him. A draped Union Jack and a Royal Marine on guard stress that Napoleon is a captive. The painting sold well and paid for Eastlake's trips to study Old Masters in Europe.

meta: Blue sea reflects off a sun-bleached rock at Appledore in Childe Hassam's Cliff Rock, painted in 1903 and bought in 1906.
about: Blue sea reflects onto a large, sun-bleached rock at Appledore, one of the nine islands of the Isles of Shoals off New Hampshire and Maine. Distant shores are hinted at with lines of cream and green, and broken brushstrokes suggest shadows and reflections in the water. Childe Hassam painted it in 1903 under the influence of French Impressionism. Appledore had a small artist colony. The John Herron Art Fund bought the picture at its first exhibition in 1906.
